s: Under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, prisons are included in which of the following?
x: Prisons are a State subject under Entry 4 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.

s: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 guides States in replacing the colonial Prisons Act of which year?
x: The MHA's Model Prisons Act, 2023 is meant to replace the Prisons Act, 1894; it is not automatically binding on States.

s: Under BNSS Section 479, an undertrial is generally eligible for release after serving what part of the maximum term?
x: BNSS Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, reduced to one-third for first-time offenders, subject to statutory conditions.

s: Which body issues advisory guidelines on prison administration, alongside the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals?
x: Prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals, while BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, what were the prison occupancy rate and the proportion of undertrials respectively?
x: NCRB Prison Statistics 2024 reported prison occupancy at 112.7%, with undertrials constituting 73% of the prison population.

s: With reference to parole and furlough, which one of the following is correct?
o: They are available only to undertrial prisoners.
They are governed by identical Central rules applicable to every State.
They are not absolute rights, and each State has its own prisoner-release rules.
They constitute an absolute constitutional right available uniformly throughout India.
x: Parole and furlough are not absolute rights. Each State frames its own prisoner-release or parole rules.

s: What is the status of the Model Prisons Act, 2023, prepared by the MHA?
o: A guide not binding on States
A Central law replacing State jail manuals
x: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 is an MHA guide for replacing the 1894 Act and is not binding, since prisons are a State subject.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, women made up what share of prison inmates?
x: Women were 4.14% of inmates, and there are only 34 women's prisons.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prisons in India?
o: Prisons fall under Entry 4 of the State List
First-time undertrials may be freed after one-third of the maximum term under BNSS s.479
The Prisons Act, 1894 is a colonial law
Parole and furlough are absolute rights of prisoners
x: Parole and furlough are not absolute rights; each State has its own rules.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, undertrials constituted approximately what share of inmates?
x: Undertrials were about 73% of inmates; women were 4.14% and there were only 34 women's prisons.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, which State/UT had the highest prison occupancy rate?
x: Delhi's prisons were the most overcrowded at 194.6% occupancy, ahead of Meghalaya (163.5%); the national rate was 112.7%.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, how many prisons were there in India?
x: NCRB Prison Statistics 2024: 1,333 prisons, capacity about 4.53 lakh and 5.11 lakh inmates.

s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, how many exclusive women's prisons does India have?
x: Women are 4.14% of inmates and India has only 34 women's prisons (NCRB Prison Statistics 2024).

s: In Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014), what was inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition held to do?
o: Justify commuting death to life imprisonment
x: The Court held that unexplained delay in deciding mercy petitions may justify commuting the death sentence to life imprisonment.

s: The decision in Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006) is associated with which proposition?
o: Mercy powers are completely immune from judicial scrutiny.
Pardon and remission are open to limited judicial review.
Only the Supreme Court may decide mercy petitions.
A Governor may pardon every death sentence.
x: Epuru Sudhakar (2006) established that the exercise of pardon or remission powers is subject to limited judicial review.

s: Which of the following pairs (case — holding) is correctly matched?
o: Bachan Singh (1980) — Categories of rarest cases
Machhi Singh (1983) — Death penalty held constitutional
Bachan Singh (1980) — 'Rarest of rare': life the rule, death the exception
x: Bachan Singh (1980) laid down 'rarest of rare'; Jagmohan Singh (1973) upheld the death penalty and Machhi Singh (1983) set categories of rarest cases.

s: By which court must a death sentence passed by a Sessions Court be confirmed?
x: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court requires confirmation by the High Court.

s: An appeal against a death sentence may reach the Supreme Court under which combination of constitutional provisions?
x: Appeals in such matters may lie to the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.

s: In which case was the 'rarest of rare' doctrine for the death penalty laid down?
x: Bachan Singh (1980) laid down 'rarest of rare', with life imprisonment as the rule.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold the death penalty to be in Jagmohan Singh (1973)?
x: Jagmohan Singh (1973) upheld the death penalty as constitutional.

s: For what is Machhi Singh (1983) known?
o: Laying down categories, weighing aggravating against mitigating factors
Delay as a ground for commutation
x: Machhi Singh (1983) set out categories of cases and the balance of aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

s: Under which Article can the President pardon a death sentence?
x: Article 72 lets the President pardon a death sentence; the Governor under Article 161 cannot.

s: Under Article 161, which of the following can the Governor NOT do to a death sentence?
x: The Governor may commute, remit or suspend a death sentence but cannot pardon it.

s: According to Amnesty International, which country is the world's biggest executioner?
x: Amnesty International reports name China as the biggest executioner in the world.

s: In Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014), how many days' notice before execution was held necessary after a mercy petition is rejected?
x: Shatrughan Chauhan (2014) required 14 days between rejection of mercy and execution, and held delay a ground for commutation.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provides the punishment for murder?
x: Murder is punishable under Section 103 of the BNS, which replaced Section 302 of the IPC.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold about the solitary confinement of death-row convicts in Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014)?
o: It is mandatory after rejection of mercy
It is allowed for up to 14 days
It is left to the Governor
x: Shatrughan Chauhan held solitary confinement illegal, allowed commutation for inordinate delay and required 14 days before execution.

s: According to Amnesty International, in how many countries were executions carried out in 2017?
x: Amnesty recorded executions in 23 countries in 2017, with China the biggest executioner.

s: According to Amnesty International's report 'Death Sentences and Executions 2025', which country carried out the most recorded executions in 2025, excluding China?
x: Amnesty's 2025 report recorded Iran as the top executioner with at least 2,159 executions, followed by Saudi Arabia. China is not counted because its figures are a state secret, though it remains the biggest executioner.

s: At least how many executions did Amnesty International record worldwide (excluding China) in 2025, its highest figure since 1981?
x: Amnesty recorded at least 2,707 executions in 17 countries in 2025, up 78% from 1,518 in 2024.

s: In cases of custodial death, information is required to be reported to the NHRC within what period?
x: Custodial deaths are to be reported to the NHRC within 24 hours; post-mortem videography and independent investigation are also associated safeguards.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the NHRC norms on custodial deaths?
o: Reporting the death to the NHRC within 24 hours
Investigation only by officers of the same police station
x: NHRC norms require a report within 24 hours, post-mortem videography and an independent investigation.

s: Which of the following case–principle pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Nilabati Behera – Compensation for custodial death
Joginder Kumar – Arrest must be justified; a relative may be informed
Arnesh Kumar – No automatic arrest for offences up to seven years
D.K. Basu – No automatic arrest for offences up to seven years
x: D.K. Basu laid down arrest safeguards like the arrest memo and medical examination; the seven-year rule is from Arnesh Kumar.

s: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory safeguard associated with D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal?
o: Automatic arrest in every offence punishable up to seven years
x: D.K. Basu required safeguards such as an arrest memo, identification of officers, informing kin and medical examination. Automatic arrest for offences up to seven years is contrary to the safeguard approach associated with Arnesh Kumar.

s: Which provision made a judicial inquiry mandatory in cases of custodial death, and what is its present BNSS equivalent?
x: CrPC Section 176(1A) made judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths; the corresponding BNSS provision is Section 196.

s: During 1999-2023, how many police-custody deaths and convictions were reported?
x: The reported data recorded 2,253 police-custody deaths and only three convictions during 1999–2023.

s: Which State records the highest number of deaths in police custody?
x: Bihar records the most police-custody deaths, followed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

s: Which case held that there is no sovereign immunity against compensation for a custodial death?
x: Nilabati Behera (1993) awarded compensation under Articles 32/226 for custodial death and rejected sovereign immunity.

s: Arnesh Kumar (2014) barred automatic arrest for offences punishable with imprisonment up to how many years?
x: Arnesh Kumar (2014) ruled out automatic arrest for offences up to 7 years (CrPC s.41, now BNSS s.35).

s: Joginder Kumar (1994) is associated with which principle?
o: No automatic arrest for offences up to 7 years
x: Joginder Kumar (1994) held that an arrest must be justified and a friend or relative informed.

s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
1. D.K. Basu
2. Arnesh Kumar
3. Nilabati Behera
4. Joginder Kumar
x: Nilabati Behera (1993), Joginder Kumar (1994), D.K. Basu (1997), Arnesh Kumar (2014).

s: Which BNSS section requires sanction before a court takes cognisance of an offence against a public servant?
x: BNSS Section 218 requires prior sanction against public servants, which can delay prosecution in custodial cases.

s: The Gade Sai Krishna custodial death case in Andhra Pradesh involved the police of which station?
x: Gade Sai Krishna died in the custody of Krishnalanka police, Vijayawada; the NHRC sought reports from the AP SHRC, DGP and Chief Secretary.

s: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down how many guidelines on encounter deaths?
x: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.

s: Under the PUCL guidelines on encounter deaths, which of the following is barred until the officers involved are cleared?
x: The guidelines require recording the tip-off, an FIR and an independent probe, and prohibit out-of-turn promotion or gallantry awards until clearance.

s: What do NHRC norms, which treat encounter deaths as serious violations, require?
o: Investigation only by the armed forces
Mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation
x: The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations requiring mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.

s: Under the PUCL (2014) guidelines, by whom is an encounter death to be independently probed?
x: PUCL requires an FIR, an independent probe by the CID, a magisterial inquiry and intimation to the NHRC/SHRC.

s: How many directives on police reform did Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006) issue?
x: Prakash Singh (2006) issued seven directives, including a State Security Commission, Police Establishment Board and Police Complaints Authorities.

s: Under the Prakash Singh (2006) directives, what tenure was the DGP selected from a UPSC panel to get?
x: The DGP was to be chosen from a UPSC panel and given a two-year tenure, not five years.

s: Under the Prakash Singh framework, who heads the State Police Complaints Authority?
x: The State PCA is headed by a retired judge and handles serious misconduct such as custodial death; PCAs exist at State and district levels.

s: Which colonial police law is still in force in India?
x: The Police Act, 1861 is still in force despite the Prakash Singh directives.

s: Which complaints does the State Police Complaints Authority look into?
o: Custodial death, rape and grievous hurt
x: The State PCA, headed by a retired judge, handles serious misconduct such as custodial death, rape and grievous hurt.

s: The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of the Seventh Schedule by a new prison list
Ratification of UNCAT and a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
Confirmation of all death sentences by the Supreme Court
x: The 273rd Law Commission Report (2017) recommended ratification of UNCAT and proposed a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.

s: Which committee focused on women prisoners and greater representation of women in the police?
x: The Krishna Iyer Committee dealt with women prisoners; Mulla covered comprehensive jail reforms and Amitava Roy overcrowding and undertrials.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Law Commission report with its subject?
o: 262nd Report (2015) — abolition of the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war
273rd Report (2017) — classification of rarest-of-rare cases under Machhi Singh
262nd Report (2015) — ratification of UNCAT and draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
273rd Report (2017) — creation of the All India Prison Service
x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. The 273rd Report concerned UNCAT ratification and a draft anti-torture Bill.

s: What did the Mulla Committee (1980-83) on jail reforms recommend?
x: The Mulla Committee recommended an All India Prison Service; women prisoners were the Krishna Iyer Committee's focus.

s: Which committee (2018) focused on prison overcrowding and undertrials?
x: The Justice Amitava Roy Committee (2018) dealt with overcrowding and undertrials.

s: The 262nd Law Commission Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty except for which crimes?
x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolition except for terrorism and waging war; the 273rd dealt with torture.

s: In which year did India sign the UN Convention against Torture (UNCAT), which it has not ratified?
x: India signed UNCAT in 1997 but has not ratified it; the 2010 Prevention of Torture Bill lapsed.

s: What happened to the Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010?
o: It passed both Houses but was returned by the President
It passed the Lok Sabha but lapsed
x: The 2010 Bill passed the Lok Sabha and lapsed; India still has no anti-torture law.

s:
Consider the following statements about India and the UN Convention against Torture:
1. India signed it in 1997 but has not ratified it.
2. The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended ratifying it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: India signed UNCAT in 1997 without ratifying, and the 273rd Report (2017) recommended ratification with a Prevention of Torture Bill.

s: By which law(s) was the Devadasi system prohibited in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988 only
both the Madras Act, 1947 and the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988
x: The practice was banned by the Madras Act of 1947 and, in Andhra Pradesh, by the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Child marriage — Marriage below the legally prescribed age
Devadasi — Dedication of girls to temples
x: Niyoga did not mean prohibition of widow remarriage; it involved a childless widow or wife bearing a son by the husband’s brother or kinsman.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Hindu Marriage Act
B. Bengal Sati Regulation
C. Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act
D. Child Marriage Restraint Act
x: The order is the Bengal Sati Regulation (1829), the Widow Remarriage Act (1856), the Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929) and the Hindu Marriage Act (1955), so the answer is B, C, D, A.

s: In which period did purdah become a prominent feature of women's lives?
x: Women had an honourable place in the early Vedic period; their status declined in the later Vedic and medieval periods, when purdah became prominent.

s: In which year was the Female Infanticide Prevention Act enacted during British rule?
x: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was passed in 1870 (APPSC 2018). 1829 is the abolition of Sati, 1856 the Widow Remarriage Act and 1929 the Sarda (Child Marriage Restraint) Act.

s: What does the custom of Niyoga refer to?
o: A childless widow or wife having a son by the husband's brother or kinsman
x: Niyoga let a childless widow or wife have a son by the husband's brother or kinsman; it was not a ban on widow remarriage.

s: In which year was Sati first prohibited by the Bengal Sati Regulation?
x: The Bengal Sati Regulation came in 1829; 1856 is the Widow Remarriage Act and 1870 the Female Infanticide Prevention Act.

s: In the Vedic period, by which term was the wife honoured as the 'better half' of her husband?
x: In the early Vedic period women had an honourable place; the wife was called 'Ardhangini' (better half).

s: Who founded the Arya Mahila Samaj?
x: Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj; the Phules founded the Satyashodhak Samaj.

s: Where and when did Kandukuri Veeresalingam perform the first widow remarriage in Telugu society?
x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam performed the first widow remarriage in Telugu society at Rajahmundry in 1881.

s: Who was the first woman teacher in India?
x: Savitribai Phule was India's first woman teacher, at the girls' school she and Jyotirao Phule opened in Pune in 1848.

s: In which year was the Widow Remarriage Act passed?
x: The Widow Remarriage Act came in 1856, linked to Vidyasagar's widow-remarriage movement.

s: Who wrote 'The High-Caste Hindu Woman' (1887), on the plight of widows?
x: Pandita Ramabai wrote 'The High-Caste Hindu Woman' (1887) on the plight of widows.

s: Who started the first girls' school at Pune in 1848?
x: Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule started the first girls' school at Pune in 1848.

s: Who wrote 'Stri Purush Tulana'?
x: Tarabai Shinde wrote Stri Purush Tulana; Jyotirao Phule wrote Gulamgiri.

s: In which year did Raja Rammohan Roy found the Brahmo Samaj?
x: Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828; sati was abolished in 1829 and the Satyashodhak Samaj came in 1873.

s: Who is the author of 'The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna'?
x: The Gospel is by Mahendranath Gupta ('M'); Ram Mohan Roy wrote 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin'.

s: Who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873?
x: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873; with Savitribai he also started the first girls' school at Pune.

s: Which social reformer is associated with the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856?
x: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned for the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

s: Who wrote 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin'?
x: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin was written by Raja Rammohan Roy, who also founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

s: With which newspaper is Raja Rammohan Roy associated?
x: Raja Rammohan Roy brought out Sambad Kaumudi; Manushi is Madhu Kishwar's journal.

s: With which school, founded in 1849 for girls' education, is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar associated?
x: Vidyasagar backed girls' education through the Bethune School (1849) and the Widow Remarriage Act, 1856.

s: Who is the author of 'Gulamgiri'?
x: Gulamgiri was written by Jyotirao Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

s: In which year did Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule open a home to prevent infanticide?
x: The Phules opened the first girls' school in Pune in 1848 and an infanticide-prevention home in 1863.

s: In which year was the Child Marriage Restraint Act, commonly known as the Sarda Act, enacted?
x: The Child Marriage Restraint or Sarda Act was enacted in 1929 and dealt with the minimum marriage age.

s: In which year was Beti Bachao Beti Padhao first launched?
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao began in 2015.

s: In which year was the National Mission for Empowerment of Women launched?
x: The Mission began in 2010, not 2015; 1992 is the NCW's set-up year.

s: Which one of the following was NOT an objective of the National Policy for Empowerment of Women, 2001?
o: Ending discrimination and violence against women
Equal access to health, education and employment
x: The 2001 policy aimed at equal access, ending violence and gender mainstreaming; commercial surrogacy was not an objective.

s: In the Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, under which area were food security and nutrition included?
x: Food security and nutrition came under health; governance and decision-making and environment were separate priority areas.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Women, created under the NCW Act, 1990, constituted?
x: The NCW is a statutory body under the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.

s: Under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, who make up the Commission besides a Chairperson and a Member-Secretary?
o: three members, at least one from the Scheduled Castes
five members, at least one each from the SCs and the STs
seven members, all nominated by the Chief Justice of India
five members, all of whom must be retired judges
x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary. The counts of three and seven are wrong, and there is no requirement that members be retired judges or nominated by the CJI.

s: India's first exclusive women's court was set up in which State?
x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal, at Malda in 2013 (APPSC 2019). Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are distractors.

s: In which year was the Family Courts Act enacted?
x: The Family Courts Act is of 1984; 953 family courts were working by July 2025.

s: Under an Act of which year was the A.P. Women's Commission set up?
x: The A.P. Women's Commission Act is of 1998 (amended 2023).

s: How was the year 2001, when the National Policy for Empowerment of Women was adopted, observed?
x: 2001 was the Year of Women's Empowerment; International Women's Year was 1975.

s: Who chairs the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women (as of December 2025)?
x: Rayapati Sailaja chairs the AP Women's Commission, set up under the A.P. Women's Commission Act, 1998.

s: As of 31 July 2025, how many Family Courts were functioning in India under the Family Courts Act, 1984?
x: There were 953 Family Courts in 29 States/UTs as of 31 July 2025.

s: In which district was India's first exclusive women's court set up in 2013?
x: India's first women's court was set up at Malda, West Bengal, in 2013.

s: In which Five-Year Plan did the approach to women shift from 'development' to 'empowerment'?
x: The Eighth Plan marked the shift from development to empowerment of women.

s: Challenges to the marital rape exception that have reached the Supreme Court concern which section of the BNS?
x: The marital rape exception under BNS Section 63 has been challenged in the Supreme Court.

s: In which year was the Indian Succession Act enacted?
x: The Indian Succession Act came in 1925, the Hindu Succession Act in 1956 and its amendment in 2005.

s: Which Act bans prenatal sex determination to stop female feticide?
x: The PCPNDT Act bans sex determination; the MTP Act allows abortion up to 24 weeks on set grounds.

s: In which year was the Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, which bans sati and its glorification, enacted?
x: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, which bans sati and its glorification, was enacted in 1987. 1829 is the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1961 the Dowry Prohibition Act and 1986 the Indecent Representation of Women Act.

s: In which year was the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act enacted?
x: It came in 1986, after the Dowry Prohibition Act (1961) and before the Commission of Sati Act (1987).

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Decision within 60 days
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 — Internal Complaints Committee at the workplace
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 — Right to Residence under Section 17
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Right to Residence under Section 17
x: Right to Residence under Section 17 belongs to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. The 2013 workplace law provides for an Internal Complaints Committee and a Local Complaints Committee in the district.

s: Which of the following pairs (law — year) is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 1994
x: The Dowry Prohibition Act dates to 1961; ITPA is 1956, PCPNDT 1994 and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 provides inheritance rights to Hindus.
The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Muslims and others.
Muslim inheritance is governed by Sharia principles under Muslim Personal Law.
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 granted daughters equal coparcenary rights.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Christians and others. Muslims follow Sharia under their personal law.

s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, an Internal Complaints Committee is required in every workplace with at least how many employees?
x: An ICC is needed at 10 or more employees; smaller workplaces are covered by a district-level Local Committee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about laws for women?
o: The Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is a civil law remedy.
The Muslim Women Act, 2019 declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat void and illegal.
The Maternity Benefit Amendment Act, 2017 mandates a crèche where there are 50 or more employees.
The PCPNDT Act, 1994 permits sex determination in ultrasound clinics.
x: The PCPNDT Act bans sex determination.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act is correctly matched?
o: Status of a child marriage – Void
x: PCMA replaced the 1929 Sarda Act; it came into force on 1 November 2007, sets 18 for females and 21 for males, and makes child marriages voidable.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829 abolished Sati.
The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1976 prohibits dowry.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides protection from domestic violence.
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 legalized widow remarriage.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Dowry Prohibition Act dates from 1961, not 1976. 1976 is the Equal Remuneration Act and the renaming of the Civil Rights Act.

s: Which of the following law–purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986 – Prevents child marriage
Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 – Equal wages for men and women
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 – Prevents child marriage
x: The Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986 prohibits indecent depiction of women; child marriage is dealt with by the 2006 Act.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Special Marriage Act commenced on January 1, 1955.
The PCPNDT Act commenced on January 1, 1994.
The Dowry Prohibition Act commenced on July 1, 1961.
x: Option B is incorrect: the PCPNDT Act was passed in 1994 but came into force on 1 January 1996. The trap mixes up the year it was passed with the year it took effect.

s: In which year was the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, which replaced the Child Marriage Restraint (Sarda) Act of 1929, enacted?
x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act was enacted in 2006 and replaced the Sarda Act, 1929. 1978 is when the Sarda Act's age limits were raised, 2012 is the POCSO Act and 2019 is the triple talaq law.

s: In which year was the Dowry Prohibition Act enacted?
x: The Dowry Prohibition Act is of 1961, not 1976 (the Equal Remuneration Act year).

s: When did the PCPNDT Act, 1994 come into force?
x: PCPNDT came into force on 1 January 1996; the other dates belong to the MTP Act, Domestic Violence Act and PCMA.

s: Which Act provides for monogamy and grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law?
x: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.

s: What does the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declare instant Talaq-e-Biddat to be?
o: Permitted when approved by a Maintenance Tribunal
Void and illegal, with imprisonment up to three years
A civil remedy through Protection Officers only
x: The 2019 Act makes instant talaq-e-biddat void and illegal and a criminal offence, punishable with up to three years in prison.

s: Which Act provides a civil, secular framework for marriage irrespective of caste, religion or faith, after public notice?
x: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides civil, secular marriage for anyone, whatever their caste, religion or faith, after a public notice.

s: Which of the following law–provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Hindu Marriage Act – Conditions of marriage, divorce and restitution of conjugal rights
Hindu Succession Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters by birth
POSH Act – Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters
x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act makes child marriages voidable; coparcenary rights come under the Hindu Succession law.

s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 is associated with which of the following?
x: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, made instant triple talaq a crime. Widow remarriage was the 1856 Act, and civil marriage the Special Marriage Act.

s: In which year did the Andhra Pradesh Assembly pass the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act under N.T. Rama Rao?
x: AP passed its amendment on 24 September 1985, after the 1956 Act and before the 2005 Central amendment.

s: Where is the secular maintenance remedy for wives, earlier under Section 125 of the CrPC (applied in Shah Bano), now found?
o: Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act
x: Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaced CrPC Section 125 as the secular maintenance route. BNS is a penal code, Section 17 of the PWDVA is the right to residence, and BNSS Section 479 concerns release of undertrials.

s: Under Section 2(2), to whom does the Hindu Succession Act not apply?
o: Members of Scheduled Tribes, unless the Central Government directs otherwise
x: Section 2(2) excludes notified Scheduled Tribes unless the Centre directs otherwise; the Supreme Court (8 Oct 2025) upheld this exclusion.

s: Which State had already made unmarried daughters coparceners through its amendment before the national Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005?
x: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the relevant Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.

s: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is associated with which of the following reforms?
o: Abolition of the female heir’s limited estate and equal inheritance for women
Mandatory registration of every inter-faith marriage under one uniform law
x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate. Civil marriage irrespective of religion is associated with the Special Marriage Act.

s: Under the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, instant talaq-e-biddat is punishable with imprisonment up to how many years?
x: The 2019 Act makes instant talaq void, illegal and a cognisable offence punishable with up to 3 years.

s: To which Article does India's reservation (as distinct from its declarations) under CEDAW relate?
x: India's reservation is on Article 29(1) (arbitration/ICJ); Articles 5(a), 16(1) and 16(2) carry declarations.

s: Which period did the UN Decade for Women cover?
x: The UN Decade for Women extended from 1976 to 1985.

s: In which year did India ratify CEDAW?
x: India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993, both before the Beijing Conference of 1995.

s: How many critical areas of concern does the Beijing Platform for Action (1995) identify?
x: The Beijing Platform for Action, adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women, identifies 12 critical areas, including the girl child.

s: Under which UN body does the UN Commission on the Status of Women (1946) function?
x: The CSW functions under ECOSOC, not the General Assembly.

s: With which venue and year were the International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women associated?
x: The International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women were held in Mexico City in 1975.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Beijing Conference was held in 1995, not 1980. Copenhagen was the second World Conference in 1980, and Nairobi was the third in 1985.

s: At which World Conference on Women was gender mainstreaming promoted globally?
x: The Fourth World Conference on Women (Beijing, 1995) promoted gender mainstreaming globally.

s:
Consider the following statements about India and CEDAW:
1. India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993.
2. India's reservation relates to Article 29(1).
3. India made declarations on Articles 5(a), 16(1) and 16(2).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: signed 1980, ratified 1993; reservation on 29(1) (arbitration/ICJ) and declarations on 5(a), 16(1), 16(2).

s: With whom is the statement that “the world's welfare is impossible unless women's condition improves; a bird cannot fly on one wing” associated?
x: This observation is associated with Swami Vivekananda.

s: Who coined the term ‘Missing women’?
x: Amartya Sen coined the term ‘missing women’ to refer to the consequences of discrimination against women, including intra-household discrimination.

s: Which of the following statement–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Progress of a community measured by the progress of its women – B.R. Ambedkar
Condition of a nation told by the status of its women – Jawaharlal Nehru
A bird cannot fly on one wing – Swami Vivekananda
'To call woman the weaker sex is a libel' – B.R. Ambedkar
x: Calling the 'weaker sex' label a libel was Mahatma Gandhi's statement.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Uma Chakravarti — A Field of One’s Own
Gail Omvedt — Seeing Like a Feminist
Bina Agarwal — Land rights and A Field of One’s Own
x: Bina Agarwal is associated with land rights and authored A Field of One’s Own. Seeing Like a Feminist is associated with Nivedita Menon, while ‘missing women’ was coined by Amartya Sen.

s: Who said 'To call woman the weaker sex is a libel'?
x: The statement is Gandhi's; Vivekananda used the 'bird on one wing' image.

s: Which of the following work–author pairs is correctly matched?
o: Seeing Like a Feminist – Amartya Sen
A Field of One's Own – Bina Agarwal
x: Bina Agarwal wrote A Field of One's Own; Seeing Like a Feminist is Nivedita Menon's, Stri Purush Tulana Tarabai Shinde's, Gulamgiri Jyotirao Phule's.

s: Which of the following statements on women is attributed to B.R. Ambedkar?
o: A bird cannot fly on one wing
I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved
To call woman the weaker sex is a libel
You can tell the condition of a nation by looking at the status of its women
x: Ambedkar measured a community's progress by the progress of its women; the other lines are Vivekananda's, Gandhi's and Nehru's.

s: Who said, 'You can tell the condition of a nation by looking at the status of its women'?
x: This statement on the status of women is Jawaharlal Nehru's.

s: Gender budgeting, equal opportunities, workplace safety and participation in decision-making are components of which type of audit?
x: All four are components of a gender audit.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stated cause of a low sex ratio?
x: Son preference, female foeticide or infanticide, dowry and neglect of girls are stated causes of a low sex ratio. Equal inheritance and universal schooling are not listed as causes.

s: What does a gender audit, a systematic evaluation of gender equality, cover?
x: A gender audit covers policies, programmes and institutions as well as budgets, not budgets alone.

s: What is a system in which men hold primary power and status in family and society called?
x: This defines patriarchy; 'unequal treatment by society of men and women' defines gender discrimination.

s: In which respects does the Gender Development Index compare females and males?
o: Health, education and command over resources
x: The GDI makes a female-to-male comparison in health, education and command over resources.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the dimensions of the Global Gender Gap Index?
x: The Global Gender Gap Index covers economic participation, education, health and survival, and political empowerment. Military expenditure is not one of its dimensions.

s: What is integrating gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions to achieve gender equality called?
x: Gender mainstreaming works toward gender equality by bringing a gender perspective into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the sex ratio figures reported by NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 respectively?
x: The sex ratio was 991 in NFHS-4 and increased to 1020 in NFHS-5.

s: Which States are the most male-skewed in sex ratio in India?
x: Haryana and Punjab are the most male-skewed; Kerala and the North-East (Arunachal, Meghalaya, Mizoram) have the best balance.

s: To which index does the 0 to 1 scale, in which 0 denotes equality and 1 the worst outcome, belong?
x: The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the Gender Inequality Index, not the GDI.

s: What was India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index 2025?
x: India was 131st of 148 in 2025 (129th in 2024); 131/177 is its Women, Peace and Security Index rank.

s: What is unequal treatment of men and women by society termed?
x: Gender discrimination is unequal treatment of men and women by society; patriarchy is men holding main power.

s: What is a check of whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally called?
x: A gender audit checks whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally; gender mainstreaming was adopted as a strategy at Beijing.

s: Which of the following statements about gender auditing is incorrect?
o: It is a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
It excludes workplace safety from its components.
It aims to improve women's participation.
x: Option C is incorrect: workplace safety is one of the components of a gender audit. The audit is a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.

s: What was India's rank in the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023?
x: India ranked 131 of 177 in the WPS Index 2023; 131 of 148 is its Global Gender Gap 2025 rank.

s: As per 'Women and Men in India 2025', India's sex ratio at birth rose from 904 in 2017-19 to what in 2021-23?
x: Sex ratio at birth improved from 904 (2017-19) to 917 (2021-23); 1020 is the NFHS-5 overall sex ratio.

s: What was the labour force participation rate of women in India in 2022-23?
x: Women's LFPR rose from 23.3% (2017-18) to 37% (2022-23).

s: Reducing gender discrimination, ensuring equitable development and promoting inclusive governance are aims of which of the following?
x: These, along with women's empowerment, are the aims of gender mainstreaming.

s: What did the Haji Ali Dargah case decided by the Bombay High Court in 2016 concern?
o: Maintenance of a divorced Muslim woman
Women's exclusion from the inner sanctum
Entry of women aged 10–50 into a temple
x: The case concerned the bar on women entering the inner sanctum of Haji Ali Dargah; entry was ultimately allowed.

s: In Rakhi Bisht v. Union of India, what did the Delhi High Court hold that maternity protection also covers?
o: Only salary and leave, excluding the post held
Appointment to a higher post irrespective of eligibility
Only promotion, but not status or posting
Post, status and promotion, with entitlement to the same or an equivalent post on return
x: The Delhi High Court held that maternity protection extends to post, status and promotion. A returning woman is entitled to the same or an equivalent post, not automatically to a higher post.

s: In which case was the right of a daughter to be a coparcener by birth recognised, irrespective of whether the father was alive on 9 September 2005?
x: Vineeta Sharma (2020) recognised that a daughter is a coparcener by birth, whether or not the father was alive on 9 September 2005.

s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 was passed after which judgment?
x: The 1986 Act followed Shah Bano (1985); the 2019 Act was a response to Shayara Bano (2017).

s: The judgment in Shah Bano (1985) is associated with which of the following issues?
o: Entry of women aged 10–50 into the Sabarimala temple
Permanent commission for women Army officers
Maintenance of a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 of the CrPC
x: The Shah Bano judgment recognised the entitlement of a divorced Muslim woman to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC and also urged the adoption of a Uniform Civil Code.

s: By what majority was the Sabarimala entry restriction on women struck down?
x: The Sabarimala bar was struck down 4:1, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting; 3:2 was Shayara Bano.

s: By what majority did the Supreme Court hold instant triple talaq unconstitutional in Shayara Bano v. Union of India?
x: Instant triple talaq was held unconstitutional by a 3:2 majority in 2017. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was enacted in 2019.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha upheld the constitutional validity of Restitution of Conjugal Rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
Danial Latifi v. Union of India held that maintenance is limited solely to the iddat period.
Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma clarified the coparcenary rights of daughters by birth.
Shayara Bano v. Union of India declared instant Talaq-e-Biddat violative of Article 14.
x: Option B is incorrect: Danial Latifi held that maintenance is not limited to the iddat period and must cover the wife's whole life.

s: Which judgment laid down binding guidelines against workplace sexual harassment that led directly to the POSH Act, 2013?
o: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha
x: Vishaka's guidelines, based on Articles 14, 19 and 21, led directly to the POSH Act, 2013.

s: Which section of the IPC did Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) strike down?
x: Section 497 (adultery) was struck down as archaic, patriarchal and against Articles 14 and 21.

s: In X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD (2022), up to how many weeks were all women, regardless of marital status, held entitled to safe and legal abortion?
x: The Court allowed abortion up to 24 weeks for all women, married or not, and counted marital rape under the MTP rules.

s: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) primarily dealt with which of the following?
o: Conversion to Islam to contract a second Hindu marriage
Adultery under Section 497 of the IPC
x: Sarla Mudgal held that conversion to Islam cannot be used to validate a second marriage by a Hindu man and stressed the need for a Uniform Civil Code.

s: With which issue is Seema v Ashwani Kumar (2006) associated?
x: Seema v Ashwani Kumar (2006) made registration of marriages compulsory.

s: What did Babita Puniya (2020) concern?
o: Permanent commission for women Short Service Commission officers in the Army
x: Babita Puniya (2020) granted permanent commission to women SSC officers in the Army.

s: How far did Danial Latifi (2001) hold that a divorced Muslim wife's maintenance extends?
o: Only until she remarries within iddat
Beyond the iddat period, for her whole life
x: Danial Latifi (2001) read the 1986 Act to require provision beyond iddat, for her whole life.

s: Who filed the petition in the Haji Ali Dargah case (Bombay HC, 2016)?
x: Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan (Zakia Soman, Noorjehan Safia Niaz) won women's entry to the inner sanctum.

s: Which of the following case–ruling pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sarla Mudgal (1995) – Permanent commission for women officers
Saroj Rani (1984) – Upheld restitution of conjugal rights
Joseph Shine (2018) – Struck down Section 497 IPC
x: Sarla Mudgal held that conversion to Islam cannot validate a second Hindu marriage; permanent commission was Babita Puniya (2020).

s: Which judge gave the lone dissent in the Sabarimala temple entry judgement of 2018?
x: The bar on women aged 10-50 was struck down 4:1; Justice Indu Malhotra was the only woman judge on the bench and dissented.

s: Who were the first women of menstruating age to enter the Sabarimala temple after the 2018 verdict?
o: Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz
x: Bindu Ammini and Kanaka Durga entered in January 2019; Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz were the Haji Ali petitioners.

s: Along with the Allahabad High Court's Rahmatullah case (1994), which 2002 Supreme Court case is cited as an early ruling against arbitrary triple talaq?
x: Before Shayara Bano (2017), Rahmatullah (Allahabad HC, 1994) and Shamim Ara (SC, 2002) held arbitrary triple talaq invalid.

s: Who founded the first Women’s Studies Centre at SNDT?
x: Neera Desai founded the first Women’s Studies Centre at SNDT.

s: In the early 20th century, to what did the focus of the Indian women's movement shift?
x: The 19th-century phase took up sati, widow remarriage and education; in the early 20th century the focus shifted to political rights.

s: Who founded the Women's Indian Association (1917) along with Annie Besant?
x: Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins founded the WIA, which worked for women's votes and the right to sit in councils.

s: In which year did the Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh begin at Dubagunta?
x: It began at Dubagunta in 1992, led to the arrack ban in 1993 and total prohibition in 1995.

s: Durgabai Deshmukh, founder of the Andhra Mahila Sabha, was also the first chairperson of which body?
o: Committee on the Status of Women in India (1974)
x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha in 1937 and was the first chair of the Central Social Welfare Board, set up in 1953. The NCW came in 1992, the Committee on the Status of Women produced Towards Equality in 1974 (Vina Mazumdar as Member-Secretary), and the AIWC is linked with Margaret Cousins.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kandukuri Veeresalingam — Women's personal and sexual freedom through the novel Stree
Raja Rammohan Roy — Abolition of Sati
Pandita Ramabai — The High-Caste Hindu Woman
x: The statement is not correctly matched. Stree was written by Chalam, while Kandukuri Veeresalingam promoted widow remarriage and women's education in Telugu society.

s: Who was the Member-Secretary of the Committee on the Status of Women in India, which produced 'Towards Equality'?
x: Vina Mazumdar was Member-Secretary; the report exposed the declining status of women and helped spark the modern women's movement.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Committee on Status of Women in India was constituted in 1971 under the chairpersonship of Phulrenu Guha.
The High-Level Committee on Status of Women was constituted in 2012 under Pam Rajput.
The Committee on Status of Women in India was constituted in 1974 under the chairpersonship of Phulrenu Guha.
The report Towards Equality was associated with the Committee on Status of Women in India.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Phulrenu Guha Committee on the Status of Women was set up in 1971. 1974 is when it published 'Towards Equality'.

s: Who headed the High-Level Committee on the Status of Women, which worked on women's empowerment?
x: Pam Rajput headed the High-Level Committee on the Status of Women (2012); J.S. Verma chaired the separate Verma Committee.

s: What were the principal areas of work of the All India Women's Conference?
o: Education, social upliftment and legal rights
x: The AIWC focused on education, social upliftment and legal rights.

s: In which year was the National Council of Women in India (NCWI) founded?
x: NCWI came in 1925, between WIA (1917) and AIWC (1927).

s: Which was the first women's organisation in India, founded in 1910?
x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910) was the first women's organisation.

s: Who chaired the Committee on the Status of Women in India (1971), which produced 'Towards Equality'?
x: Phulrenu Guha chaired the committee; Vina Mazumdar was its Member-Secretary.

s: With what is Gudipati Venkata Chalam's novel 'Stree' concerned?
x: Chalam's 'Stree' argued for women's personal and sexual freedom.

s: Who founded the All India Women's Conference in 1927?
x: Margaret Cousins founded the AIWC in 1927; she had also co-founded the Women's Indian Association in 1917 with Annie Besant.

s: Which committee reviewed the laws on sexual violence in 2013, after the Nirbhaya case?
x: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee (2013) reviewed sexual violence laws, leading to the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.

s: With which journal is Madhu Kishwar associated?
x: Madhu Kishwar founded the women's journal Manushi in the post-1970s women's movement.

s: In which year did Durgabai Deshmukh found the Andhra Mahila Sabha?
x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha in 1937; she later chaired the Central Social Welfare Board (1953).

s: Which institution is associated with Vina Mazumdar?
x: Vina Mazumdar is linked with CWDS; Neera Desai set up the SNDT Women's Studies Centre and Madhu Kishwar Manushi.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is Dubagunta, where the Anti-Arrack Movement began in 1992?
x: The Anti-Arrack Movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta in Nellore district among literacy-campaign women.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It led to a ban on arrack in 1993.
2. Total prohibition followed in 1995.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 1992 movement led to an arrack ban in 1993 and to prohibition in 1995.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for special provisions for women and children?
x: Article 15(3) enables the State to make special provisions for women and children.

s: Under which Article is reservation of seats for women in Panchayats provided?
x: Article 243D covers Panchayats; 243T covers Municipalities and 330A/332A cover the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

s: What is the share of women's reservation in panchayats and municipalities in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh reserves 50% in panchayats and municipalities, above the constitutional one-third floor.

s: What is the share of women's horizontal reservation in direct recruitment in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The horizontal reservation is 33 1/3%; women get 50% of nominated posts and work contracts.

s: In the Legislative Assemblies of which UTs did the 33% women's quota under the 106th Constitutional Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) come into effect on 17 April 2026?
x: The 33% quota came into effect in the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies on 17 April 2026. Ladakh has no legislature, and neither Delhi nor the States named are the ones where it took effect on that date.

s: What happened to the Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 on 17 April 2026?
o: It was defeated by the Opposition
It was ratified by half the States
x: The Bill, which sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats to speed up the 33% women's quota, was defeated on 17 April 2026.

s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 reserves what share of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly?
x: The 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) reserves 33% (one-third) of seats for women.

s: By what name is the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 also known?
x: The 106th Amendment Act, 2023 is the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, reserving one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for women.

s: Which Article directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for men and women?
x: Article 39(d) is equal pay; 39(a) is livelihood and 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief.

s: Which Article provides for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
x: Article 42 covers humane work conditions and maternity relief; Article 44 is the Uniform Civil Code.

s: Which Article contains the Fundamental Duty to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women?
x: Article 51A(e) asks citizens to renounce practices derogatory to women's dignity.

s: In which bodies do Articles 330A and 332A reserve one-third seats for women?
x: Articles 330A/332A cover the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; 243D/243T cover Panchayats and Municipalities.

s: Under which Article is reservation of at least one-third seats for women in Municipalities provided?
x: Article 243T covers Municipalities; 243D covers Panchayats.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. Its quota in the Lok Sabha awaits the Census and delimitation.
2. It reserves one-half of the seats in the Lok Sabha for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: the Act reserves one-third (33%), not one-half, and waits for the Census and delimitation.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, what share of nominated posts and work contracts is reserved for women (April 2026)?
x: AP reserves 50% of nominated posts and work contracts for women; 33⅓% is the horizontal quota in direct recruitment.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243D — reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats
Article 42 — reservation of seats in State Assemblies
x: Article 243D provides for at least one-third reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats. Article 243T relates to Municipalities.

s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens?
x: Article 44, a Directive Principle, asks the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code.

s: Approximately what share of elected representatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions are women (January 2026)?
x: Though 243D reserves at least one-third, about 46% of PRI representatives are women.

s: Which of the following does the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021 prohibit?
o: Termination up to 20 weeks on one doctor's opinion
Termination up to 24 weeks for special categories
Termination beyond 24 weeks for substantial foetal abnormality with State Medical Board approval
x: The Act prohibits disclosure of the woman's identity; the other three are permitted.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: National registry — Regulatory record of ART institutions
Sale of gametes or embryos — Prohibited
x: Sex-selective ART is prohibited under the ART Act, 2021. Registered clinics and banks and a national registry are permitted regulatory arrangements.

s: Which of the following pairs (Act — year) is correctly matched?
x: The MTP Act dates from 1971; the Special Marriage Act is 1954, the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 and the Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.

s: When did the MTP Act, enacted in 1971, come into force?
x: The MTP Act was passed in 1971 and came into force on 1 April 1972.

s: Under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021, how many times can a woman act as a surrogate?
o: Any number of times with written consent
x: A woman can be a surrogate only once; commercial surrogacy and sex selection are prohibited.

s: A foetus carried through surrogacy may be aborted under the applicable law only when
o: the intending couple alone gives consent
the ART clinic recommends it without further approval
the surrogate gives written consent and authorisation is obtained under the MTP Act
the surrogate’s consent is specifically excluded
x: Abortion of a surrogate foetus is not prohibited outright. It requires the surrogate’s written consent and authorisation under the MTP Act.

s: Which type of surrogacy alone does the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 permit?
o: Surrogacy by the same woman more than once
x: Only altruistic surrogacy (medical costs, insurance) is allowed; commercial surrogacy and sex selection are prohibited.

s: Which of the following is prohibited under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
x: The ART Act requires registered clinics, banks and a national registry, and prohibits sex-selective ART and sale of gametes.

s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, which body handles complaints at the district level?
x: Workplaces with 10 or more employees have an Internal Complaints Committee; the Local Committee works at the district level.

s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.

s: What is SHe-Box 2.0 under Mission Shakti?
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.

s: Which of the following pairs under the POSH Act is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Internal Committee – Workplace with 10 or more employees
Local Committee – Workplace with fewer than 10 employees
Local Committee establishing authority – District Officer
Internal Committee Presiding Officer – District Officer
x: The Internal Committee is presided over by a senior woman employee; the District Officer constitutes the Local Committee.

s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, an Internal Committee must be set up at every workplace with at least how many employees?
x: An Internal Committee is required at every workplace with 10 or more employees; smaller ones are served by the Local Committee.

s: Who constitutes the Local Committee at the district level under the POSH Act, 2013?
x: The District Officer sets up the Local Committee for workplaces with fewer than 10 employees or complaints against the employer.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Internal Committee under the POSH Act, 2013?
o: It is presided over by a senior woman employee
At least half its members are women
It is constituted by the District Officer
x: The District Officer constitutes the Local Committee; the Internal Committee is set up at the workplace, headed by a senior woman employee.

s: Under the POSH Act, within how many days must the employer act on the inquiry report?
x: The inquiry must finish in 90 days and the employer must act within 60 days; complaints are made within 3 months.

s: The guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in which case led to the POSH Act, 2013?
o: Shakti Vahini v. Union of India
x: In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) the Supreme Court laid down workplace sexual-harassment guidelines, which the POSH Act, 2013 later replaced with a law.

s: What is the full name of the POSH Act, 2013?
o: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
Protection of Women from Sexual Harassment (Prohibition and Punishment) Act, 2013
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention and Rehabilitation) Act, 2013
Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women (Redressal and Compensation) Act, 2013
x: POSH stands for the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

s: Under the POSH Act, how is showing pornography treated?
o: Outside the Act's definition of harassment
Harassment only if accompanied by physical contact
Itself a form of sexual harassment
Harassment only if a demand for sexual favours is also made
x: Showing pornography is itself listed as a form of sexual harassment, along with unwelcome contact and demands for sexual favours.

s: What is the minimum punishment under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 for giving or taking dowry?
o: 5 years and fine of ₹15,000 or the value of dowry, whichever is more
x: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 prescribes at least 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of ₹15,000 or the dowry's value.

s: Which of the following Acts came into force on 1 July 1961?
x: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on 1 July 1961; ITPA is of 1956, the Sati Act of 1987 and the Indecent Representation Act of 1986.

s: Under Section 8A of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, on whom does the burden of proof lie?
x: Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused; the offences are also cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.

s: What does the term 'dowry' mean under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Only property demanded by the bride’s family before marriage
Property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage
Any gift exchanged between the spouses after marriage, including mahr
Only cash or movable property given after marriage
x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage. Dower or mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded.

s: What is the punishment for demanding dowry under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
x: Demanding dowry attracts six months to two years; giving or taking dowry (s.3) carries a minimum of five years.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Section 3 — Giving, taking or abetting dowry
Section 8A — Burden of proof on the accused
Section 8B — Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the Central Government
x: Section 8B provides for Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government, not the Central Government. Sections 3, 4 and 8A are correctly matched.

s: Which of the following is a key reason why anti-dowry laws remain ineffective?
o: Absence of any statutory prohibition of dowry
Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and disguising cases as accidents or suicides
Excessive conviction rates in dowry cases
Exclusive jurisdiction of civil courts over dowry deaths
x: Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and presenting dowry deaths as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.

s: Which of the following States are identified as leading in the incidence of dowry deaths?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are identified as the leading States in the cited assessment.

s: What is the punishment for giving or taking dowry under Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
x: Section 3 prescribes a minimum of 5 years plus fine; 6 months to 2 years is the Section 4 penalty for demanding dowry.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the definition of 'dowry' under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Property given after marriage in connection with it
Valuable security agreed to be given before marriage
Property given indirectly at the marriage
x: Dowry covers property given before, at or after marriage, directly or indirectly, but dower or mahr is excluded.

s: Which amendment of the Dowry Prohibition Act brought dowry death and its presumption into the IPC and Evidence Act?
x: The Act was amended in 1984 and 1986; the 1986 amendment brought dowry death (IPC 304B) and its presumption (Evidence Act 113B).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: The burden of proof lies on the accused
x: Dowry offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable, so 'compoundable' is wrong.

s: Who appoints Dowry Prohibition Officers under Section 8B of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
x: Section 8B provides for Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government.

s: Under which Section of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is the Right to Residence provided?
x: Section 17 gives the Right to Residence; the Act is a civil remedy in force from 26 October 2006.

s: What kind of law is the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?
x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.

s: Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers which forms of abuse?
o: Physical, sexual and verbal or emotional abuse only
Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
Physical, verbal and economic abuse only
x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.

s: Under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which pair (relief — section) is correctly matched?
x: Residence orders are under Section 19; protection orders are under Section 18, monetary relief under Section 20 and compensation orders under Section 22.

s: Who appoints Protection Officers under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?
x: The State Government appoints them; in AP, DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs act as Protection Officers, while 55 NGOs are Service Providers.

s: Who are the Protection Officers under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 in Andhra Pradesh?
x: In AP, the DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs serve as Protection Officers, with 55 NGOs as Service Providers.

s: When did the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 come into force?
x: The PWDVA was enacted in 2005 but came into force on 26 October 2006.

s: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, who grants reliefs such as protection and residence orders?
x: Protection Officers and Service Providers assist the victim, but the reliefs are granted by the Magistrate.

s: When did the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 come into force?
x: The PCMA, 2006, which replaced the Sarda Act, came into force on 1 November 2007.

s: In which year was the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, originally known as SITA, amended and renamed?
x: The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment. 1986 is the amendment year, not the enactment year; 1961, 1994 and 2003 relate to the Dowry Act, PNDT Act and its renaming.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 2006
Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987; came into force in 1988
x: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1987 and came into force in 1988. The Indecent Representation Act dates to 1986, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act to 2006 and the Muslim Women Act concerning triple talaq to 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Monitoring under the Indecent Representation law excludes digital and AI-generated content.
The Indecent Representation of Women Act bans denigrating depiction of women in advertisements and publications.
The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati.
A District Magistrate may seize property used for glorification of sati.
x: As of 2025, monitoring under the Indecent Representation law extends to digital and AI-generated content.

s: In which year was the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, originally the SITA, enacted?
x: It was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act; 1986 is only the amendment that renamed it ITPA.

s: Which of the following pairs (law – year) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act is of 2006, not 2005; the other pairs are correct.

s: Under the Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, who may seize property used for the glorification of sati?
x: The Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati, and the DM may seize property used for glorification.

s: In which year did the Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, 1987 come into force?
x: The Sati Act was enacted in 1987 and came into force in 1988.

s: When did the POSH Act, 2013 come into force?
x: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 came into force in December 2013.

s: When did the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 come into force?
x: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act was passed in 2017 and came into force on 1 April 2017.

s: Which of the following enactments was NOT absorbed into the Code on Wages, 2019?
x: The Code on Wages, 2019 absorbed the Equal Remuneration Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act and Payment of Bonus Act. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 was not among these four enactments.

s: Under the OSH Code, 2020, women may work before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when
o: the work is performed only in government offices
the employer gives permission without any further condition
they consent and prescribed safety safeguards are provided
the worker has completed ten years of service
x: The OSH Code, 2020 permits women to work during these hours with their consent and subject to safety safeguards.

s: What was the paid maternity leave under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961?
o: 26 weeks for all establishments irrespective of size
8 weeks for establishments with 20 or more employees
16 weeks for establishments with 50 or more employees
12 weeks for establishments with 10 or more employees
x: The 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid maternity leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.

s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, what is the maternity benefit for the third child onwards?
x: The 2017 position provides 12 weeks of maternity benefit for the third child onwards. The longer period applies to the first two children.

s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, for how long is a woman adopting a child below three months of age entitled to maternity benefit?
o: Six weeks from the date of adoption
Twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over to her
Twenty-six weeks from the date of adoption in every case
Eight weeks before the adoption and four weeks after it
x: An adopting mother of a child below three months is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her. The same 12-week period applies to a commissioning mother.

s: In an establishment of what size is a crèche facility mandatory under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017?
o: 20 or more employees, with two visits a day
100 or more employees, with one visit a day
30 or more employees, with three visits a day
50 or more employees, with four visits a day
x: The amendment requires a crèche in establishments having 50 or more employees. The woman is to be allowed four visits a day to the crèche.

s: Which of the following law–feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PCPNDT Act, 1994 – Regulation of ultrasound clinics
Domestic Violence Act, 2005 – Protection orders, residence rights and maintenance
Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 – Regulation of ultrasound clinics
x: The 2017 Maternity amendment raised paid maternity leave to 26 weeks; ultrasound clinics are regulated by the PCPNDT Act.

s: Of the 26 weeks under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, at most how many may be taken before delivery?
x: Up to 8 of the 26 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery.

s: Which was India's first equal pay law?
x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 (Art. 39(d)) was the first equal pay law; it is now subsumed in the Code on Wages, 2019.

s: Under the 2017 amendment, on what basis is work from home after maternity leave allowed?
o: By mutual agreement with the employer
x: The 2017 amendment allows work from home by mutual agreement.

s: Which of the following Acts does the Code on Wages, 2019 subsume?
x: The Code subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act (along with the Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Payment of Bonus Acts) and provides a statutory floor wage.

s: How many weeks of maternity leave are given for the first two children under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017?
x: The 2017 amendment raised leave for the first two children from 12 to 26 weeks.

s: How many weeks of maternity leave is a commissioning mother entitled to under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017?
x: Adoptive mothers of a child below 3 months and commissioning mothers get 12 weeks, not 26.

s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, a creche is mandatory in establishments with at least how many employees?
x: From 1 July 2017, establishments with 50 or more employees must provide a creche.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017:
1. Leave from the third child onwards is 12 weeks.
2. The employer must allow work from home after the leave in every case.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the employer may allow work from home after the leave by mutual agreement.

s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, an adoptive mother gets 12 weeks' leave when she adopts a child below what age?
x: An adoptive mother of a child below 3 months, and a commissioning mother, get 12 weeks of leave.

s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 does NOT make which of the following an offence?
o: Living on the earnings of prostitution
x: The ITPA penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution, but not prostitution itself.

s: Which of the following is correct about the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: Criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance
Only regulates registration of protective homes
Penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings, but not prostitution itself
x: The ITPA does not criminalise prostitution itself; it penalises brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting and detaining persons.

s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.

s: Which tier of the US Trafficking in Persons Report is the only one fully meeting the minimum standards?
x: Only Tier 1 fully meets the US minimum standards; Tier 2 countries are making significant efforts without fully meeting them.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the definition of trafficking under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013?
o: It applies only where the victim did not consent
x: The CLA 2013 definition covers all forms of trafficking irrespective of the victim's consent, so the consent condition is false.

s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional safeguards against exploitation:
1. Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour.
2. Article 24 bars children below 14 from factories, mines and hazardous work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Article 23 covers trafficking, begar and forced labour; Article 24 bars child labour below 14 in hazardous work.

s: Which of the following is NOT punishable under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: Living on the earnings of prostitution
x: ITPA does not punish prostitution itself; it punishes brothel-keeping, soliciting, living on earnings and detaining persons.

s: What are the punishments for an acid attack and for its attempt, respectively, under BNS Section 124?
o: Minimum ten years to life; five to seven years
Maximum three years; seven to ten years
Minimum seven years to life; five to seven years
Minimum ten years to life; one year
x: BNS Section 124 provides a minimum of ten years extending to life for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.

s: Dowry death (old IPC Section 304B) is covered under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Dowry death is BNS Section 80 (IPC 304B). Sections 85-86 cover cruelty (IPC 498A); the presumption is BSA Section 118.

s: For the purpose of the offence of dowry death, death occurring within what period from the date of marriage is specifically relevant?
x: BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs within seven years of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita deals with stalking?
x: Stalking is BNS 78 (IPC 354D); voyeurism is 77, sexual harassment 75 and outraging modesty 74.

s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita deals with acid attack?
x: Acid attack is Section 124; rape is 63-64, trafficking 143 and selling or buying minors for prostitution 98-99.

s: Trafficking of persons is covered under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Trafficking is under BNS Section 143; Section 124 concerns acid attack.

s: Voyeurism (old IPC Section 354C) is dealt with under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Voyeurism is BNS Section 77; 75 is sexual harassment, 78 stalking and 74 outraging modesty.

s: Sexual harassment (old IPC Section 354A) corresponds to which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Sexual harassment is BNS Section 75, corresponding to IPC 354A.

s: When did the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 come into force?
x: The BNS offences against women apply from 1 July 2024.

s: Rape is dealt with under which Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
x: BNS Sections 63-64 deal with rape, replacing IPC Sections 375-376.

s: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deals with the presumption of dowry death?
x: BSA Section 118 replaces Section 113B of the Evidence Act on presumption of dowry death.

s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the directions relating to the sale of acid in Laxmi v Union of India?
o: Maintenance of a register by sellers
No sale to persons below 18 years
Sale without recording the purchaser’s purpose
