x: The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted. The directions also included photo identification, a register and prohibition of sale to persons below 18 years.

s: Under which law is acid-attack injury listed as a disability?
o: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
x: The RPwD Act 2016 lists acid-attack injury as a disability.

s: What did the Ujjawala scheme, launched in 2007, cover?
o: Prosecution and conviction of traffickers only
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
Overseas employment and migration of women
x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.

s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.

s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.

s: Since when have One Stop Centres (Sakhi), funded by the Nirbhaya Fund, been functioning?
x: One Stop Centres began on 1 April 2015 under the Nirbhaya Fund, giving shelter, police, legal and medical help under one roof.

s: As of 31 July 2025, how many Fast Track Special Courts were functional in India?
x: 743 FTSCs were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts.

s: Under whom do the district Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) work?
x: AHTUs are district police units under an SP/DSP.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in crimes against women in Crime in India 2023?
x: AP recorded 22,418 cases in 2023 and ranked 11th in India.

s: Along with zero tolerance to atrocities against women, what do the Trishul committees of Andhra Pradesh aim at?
o: Zero dropouts and zero child labour
Zero drugs and zero road accidents
Zero dowry and zero child marriage
x: Trishul committees are State and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.

s: The further 4.4% fall in crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh was credited to Shakti Teams, Women's Safety Week rallies and which of the following?
o: Replacing all police stations with women police stations
Death sentences under the Disha Act
x: The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women's Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets; the Disha Act is not in force.

s: Why does the Disha Act require the assent of the President of India?
o: It seeks to amend the Constitution.
It deals with subjects exclusively placed in the Union List.
It creates a new High Court in Andhra Pradesh.
Criminal law is included in the Concurrent List.
x: The Disha Act requires Presidential assent because criminal law falls in the Concurrent List. It has not come into force as passed.

s: The Disha Bill of Andhra Pradesh was introduced mainly in response to which case?
x: The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case.

s: What is the time limit for investigation and trial of rape cases under the Disha Bill?
o: Investigation in 14 days and trial in 7 days
Investigation in 14 days and trial in 21 days
Investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days
Investigation in 21 days and trial in 14 days
x: The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.

s: The number of crimes against women reported in Andhra Pradesh declined from 25,503 in 2022 to 22,418 in 2023 and to how many in 2024?
x: Crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh fell to 19,952 in 2024, from 22,418 in 2023 and 25,503 in 2022. 17,149 is the number of arrests, not cases.

s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh women-safety initiatives is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Disha App – SOS alerts for women in distress
Abhay pilot – Implemented by Chittoor police
Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi – Women-protection functionaries in village and ward secretariats
Abhayam – Chittoor police awareness campaign for women and children
x: The Abhay pilot (free pick-up and drop for stranded women) was implemented by Prakasam police at Ongole; Abhayam was the Chittoor campaign.

s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the provisions of the Disha Act?
o: Mandatory forensic evidence in relevant cases
Death sentence for rape and gang rape
Penalties for cyber-stalking and deepfake misuse
A special court only at the State capital
x: The Disha Act provides for a special court in every district, not merely one special court at the State capital.

s: In 2022, which district of Andhra Pradesh recorded the most rape cases?
x: Visakhapatnam had the most rape cases (69), followed by NTR district (51).

s: What was the conviction rate for crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh in 2021?
x: AP's rate was 5.6%, among the lowest, against India's 26.5%; 86.7% was AP's pendency.

s: Where was 'Abhay', offering free pick-up and drop for women from 9 pm to 5 am, started?
x: Abhay is the Prakasam (Ongole) ride scheme; Abhayam is the Chittoor awareness campaign.

s: Abhayam, launched in December 2019, was an awareness campaign of which district?
x: Abhayam was a Chittoor awareness campaign; Abhay is the Ongole pick-up scheme.

s: Where do the Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi of Andhra Pradesh work as women-protection functionaries?
x: Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi work in village and ward secretariats.

s: What is the main purpose of the Disha App of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Sending SOS alerts to the police along with the user's location
Tracking investigation deadlines in sexual offences
Free pick-up and drop for women at night
x: The Disha App is an SOS app: it alerts the police and shares the woman's location.

s: How many Disha police stations (women's police stations) were set up in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh set up 18 Disha police stations as women's police stations.

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh pass the Disha Bill?
x: The AP Disha Bill was passed in December 2019 after the Hyderabad veterinarian case.

s: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in which case?
o: Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Shakti Vahini v Union of India
x: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in Lillu v State in 2013.

s: Which offence is dealt with under Section 354C of the IPC?
x: Section 354C covers voyeurism; 326A is acid attack, 326B attempt to acid attack and 354D stalking.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 2013 criminal law amendments?
x: Disrobing was provided under Section 354B IPC, not Section 354E. Sections 354A, 354C and 354D relate respectively to sexual harassment, voyeurism and stalking.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding rape under the 2013 amendment is correct?
o: Rape was confined to penile-vaginal penetration.
Penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts were included, with a minimum punishment of seven years.
The minimum punishment was reduced to five years.
Only consensual acts involving adults were covered.
x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, while keeping the minimum punishment at seven years (it was raised to ten years in 2018).

s: The 2013 provision on death for repeat rapists (IPC 376E) now corresponds to which section of the BNS?
x: IPC 376E is now BNS 71; acid attack is 124(1), sexual harassment 75 and stalking 78.

s: Which of the following was a principal policy outcome of the December 2012 Nirbhaya case?
x: The Nirbhaya outcomes were the Verma Committee, CLA 2013, the Nirbhaya Fund and the JJ Act 2015; the BNS was not one of them.

s: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee recommended keeping the age of consent at 16; at what age did Parliament fix it?
x: The Committee recommended retaining 16 years (and opposed death for rape and sought criminalising marital rape); Parliament chose 18.

s: For which crimes does the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permit 16-18-year-olds to be tried as adults?
x: The JJ Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for heinous crimes, subject to the statutory process.

s: Besides Justice J.S. Verma, who were the members of the Verma Committee?
x: The members were J.S. Verma, Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium.

s: What minimum punishment for rape was fixed by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013?
x: CLA 2013 fixed a minimum of 7 years; CLA 2018 raised it to 10 years.

s: Which of the following pairs (IPC section added in 2013 – offence) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: 354C is voyeurism; sexual harassment is 354A.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice J.S. Verma Committee:
1. It recommended criminalising marital rape.
2. It recommended the death penalty for rape.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape but did not recommend the death penalty for rape.

s: In which month and year did the Justice J.S. Verma Committee submit its report?
x: Set up after the December 2012 Nirbhaya case, the Verma Committee reported in January 2013.

s: The 'Nirbhay Raho' initiative under the Nirbhaya Fund brings together the Panchayati Raj Ministry, the Ministry of Women and Child Development and which institution?
x: Nirbhay Raho joins the Panchayati Raj Ministry, MWCD and NLSIU under the Nirbhaya Fund.

s: Acid attack under IPC Section 326A now corresponds to which BNS provision?
x: 326A acid attack is BNS 124(1); 326B attempted acid attack is 124(2).

s: In which year was the Nirbhaya Fund set up?
x: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in 2013 as a dedicated corpus for projects related to women’s safety.

s: From which fund are One Stop Centres (Sakhi) for women funded?
x: One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181 and ERSS 112 are all funded by the Nirbhaya Fund.

s: Which of the following is included in the Safe City Projects?
o: A national database of convicted sexual offenders
Free transport for women stranded at night in rural areas
CCTV and AI-based public safety measures for women in eight major cities
Only the construction of women’s prisons in every district
x: Safe City Projects use CCTV and artificial intelligence-based public-safety measures for women in eight major cities.

s: Which of the following correctly describes Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs)?
o: State-level relief homes for trafficked women under Mission Shakti
Special courts for trafficking trials in each district
Central units of I4C issuing cyber-trafficking alerts
District-level task forces funded by MHA for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution
x: AHTUs are district-level task forces funded by the Ministry of Home Affairs for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nirbhaya Fund – created after the 2019 Hyderabad case
x: ERSS uses the single emergency number 112. The women helpline is 181, the cyber helpline 1930, and the Nirbhaya Fund followed the 2012 Delhi case.

s: From which fund are Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 funded?
x: Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 receive funding from the Nirbhaya Fund, which is dedicated to women’s-safety projects.

s: How does the Central Victim Compensation Fund (MHA, 2015) support State victim-compensation schemes?
o: A one-time grant from the Nirbhaya Fund
x: The CVCF received a one-time grant from the Nirbhaya Fund to support State schemes.

s:
Assertion (A): SHe-Box helps streamline redressal under the POSH Act.
Reason (R): A complaint filed on SHe-Box goes directly to the Internal or Local Committee that has jurisdiction over it.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: SHe-Box (Sexual Harassment electronic Box) is an online portal whose complaints are routed directly to the Internal or Local Committee concerned, which is how it speeds redressal under the POSH Act. R explains A.

s: From which fund are Mahila Police Volunteers supported?
x: Mahila Police Volunteers, a joint MWCD-MHA initiative, are funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.

s: What is the number of the Women Helpline that is being integrated with ERSS-112?
x: Women Helpline 181, universalised in 2015 and funded by the Nirbhaya Fund, is being integrated with ERSS-112.

s: What is the full form of SHe-Box?
x: SHe-Box is the Sexual Harassment electronic Box for online complaints under the POSH Act.

s: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline function under which organisation for reporting cybercrime?
o: CERT-In under the Ministry of Communications
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre under the Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for Women under the Ministry of Women and Child Development
National Crime Records Bureau under the Ministry of Law and Justice
x: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline operate under the Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The portal particularly facilitates reporting of crimes such as CSAM and non-consensual imagery against women and children.

s: Which cases are mainly dealt with by the Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund?
o: Only cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act
x: The FTSC scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund for cases involving rape and offences under POCSO.

s: Which system of the NCRB links police stations across the country?
x: CCTNS links police stations nationwide; NDSO is the database of convicted sexual offenders.

s: Under the POCSO Act, which court may be designated as the Special Court in each district?
o: Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate
x: The POCSO Act permits a Sessions Court to be designated as the Special Court in each district.

s: Which system tracks the two-month deadline for investigation of sexual offences?
x: ITSSO (BPR&D) tracks investigations; NDSO is the offender database.

s: Which body maintains the National Database on Sexual Offenders (2018)?
x: NDSO is maintained by the NCRB and holds data on convicted sexual offenders for police use.

s: In which year was the Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) scheme launched?
x: The FTSC scheme (2019) followed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.

s: Which State announced 45 fast-track courts in December 2019?
x: Odisha announced 45 fast-track courts in December 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about fast-track courts:
1. They were created by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.
2. The FTSC scheme followed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Fast-track courts are administrative and were not created by CLA 2013, so 1 is wrong; the FTSC scheme followed CLA 2018.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: NDSO is a national database of sexual offenders maintained by the NCRB.
ITSSO ensures mandatory two-month investigation completion in rape cases.
ITSSO is a citizen portal for reporting online financial fraud.
ITSSO provides real-time monitoring of investigations in sexual-offence cases.
x: Option C is incorrect: ITSSO is a police tool for tracking sexual-offence investigations against the two-month deadline. Citizens report financial fraud on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.

s: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under Section 103 of the BNS.

s: Which of the following punishment changes was made by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
o: Anticipatory bail became mandatory in rape cases involving minors.
All offences against children were made compoundable.
The minimum punishment for rape was reduced from seven to five years.
The minimum punishment for rape was raised from seven to ten years.
x: The 2018 amendment raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven years to ten years.

s: What is the minimum punishment for rape of a girl below 16 years under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
x: The 2018 Act set a 20-year minimum for rape of a girl under 16; rape of a girl under 12 carries 20 years to life or death.

s: Which section of the BNS deals with sexual intercourse by deceitful means, such as a false promise of marriage or job?
x: BNS Section 69 is the new offence of intercourse by deceitful means, including false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud.

s: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita raises the age for the gang-rape provision from 16 to how many years?
x: The BNS raises the age from 16 to 18 while retaining the IPC provisions on rape, stalking and voyeurism.

s: What is the punishment for rape of a girl below 12 years under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
x: For a girl under 12 the punishment is 20 years to life or death; for under 16 the minimum is 20 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. It raised the minimum punishment for rape from 7 to 10 years.
2. It bars anticipatory bail for rape of a girl below 16.
3. It allows 6 months for investigation of rape.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: investigation must end in 2 months; 6 months is for appeals.

s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 was enacted in the context of which cases?
x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the Kathua and Unnao cases and was associated with the fast-track court response.

s: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which principle applies to trafficking?
o: Consent is relevant only if the trafficking is inter-State.
The victim’s consent is always a complete defence.
Consent matters only when the victim is an adult male.
x: Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.

s: Which provision of the Constitution of India prohibits traffic in human beings?
x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. Article 21A is the right to education, Article 24 bars child labour in hazardous employment, and Article 39(f) is a Directive Principle on protecting children from exploitation.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 24 – Prohibits traffic in human beings
Palermo Protocol – Supplements the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime
BNS Section 143 – Victim's consent is necessary
2021 draft trafficking Bill – CBI as national investigating agency
x: The Palermo Protocol supplements UNTOC and addresses trafficking, especially of women and children; India has ratified it. Traffic in human beings is Article 23, consent is immaterial under s.143, and the 2021 draft named the NIA.

s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: Prostitution itself is treated as a crime in every circumstance.
Only trafficking of children is punishable.
Brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution are punishable acts.
The Act abolishes protective homes maintained by State Governments.
x: The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.

s: What happened to the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018?
o: It was passed by the Lok Sabha but lapsed
It was passed by both Houses and became an Act
It was passed only by the Rajya Sabha
It was rejected by the Lok Sabha
x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha and later lapsed; the NIA proposal came in the 2021 draft Bill.

s: According to UNODC's Global Report on Trafficking in Persons 2016, what do victims and traffickers often have in common?
x: GLOTIP 2016 found that victims and traffickers often share the same background.

s: The 2021 draft trafficking Bill proposed which body as the national investigating agency?
x: The 2021 draft Bill named the NIA as the national investigating agency.

s: In which year was the Palermo Protocol on trafficking in persons adopted?
x: The Palermo Protocol (2000) supplements UNTOC and targets trafficking, especially of women and children.

s: Honour killings violate which of the following sets of Articles?
x: Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, which protect equality, freedoms and life and personal liberty.

s: What did the Supreme Court judgment in Shakti Vahini v Union of India (2018) mainly deal with?
o: interference by khaps in marriages of consenting adults
the two-finger test in rape cases
x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.

s: The Law Commission's 242nd Report (2012) proposed a draft law on which subject?
o: Interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour
x: The 242nd Report proposed a draft law against interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour.

s: In Laxmi v. Union of India (2013), against what may acid be sold over the counter?
o: Photo ID and the stated purpose
x: The SC allowed sale only against photo ID and a recorded purpose, with a register and no sale to under-18s.

s: The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 is enforced under which Article until a law is made?
x: The Witness Protection Scheme 2018 is enforced under Article 141 till a law is made.

s: Which of the following pairs (crime head — NCRB classification) is correctly matched?
o: Cruelty by husband or relatives — Special and Local Law
Kidnapping and abduction of women — Special and Local Law
Indecent representation of women — Special and Local Law
Protection of women from domestic violence — IPC/BNS head
x: Indecent representation and domestic violence (PWDVA) are SLL heads; cruelty by husband and kidnapping/abduction are IPC/BNS heads.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of crimes against women?
o: Patriarchal norms and son preference reinforce unequal power relations.
Alcoholism and aggression among partners or parents may contribute to violence.
Dowry demands have no link with bride burning.
Some aggressors were themselves abused as children.
x: Dowry demands are listed as a cause that may escalate into bride burning.

s: Which of the following contributes to under-reporting of violence against women?
o: A large share of women in the police
x: Stigma, fear, lack of awareness and economic dependence cause under-reporting; conviction rates are low and pendency high.

s: Where was the first all-women police station in India set up?
x: The first all-women police station was established at Kozhikode in Kerala in 1973.

s: In which State was India's first women's court set up?
x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal (APPSC-GS 2019). Kerala had the first all-women police station (Kozhikode, 1973), Odisha announced 45 fast-track courts in 2019, and Andhra Pradesh is linked to the Disha model, so those options are traps.

s: Which of the following is a Special and Local Laws (SLL) crime head rather than an IPC/BNS head?
o: Offences under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005
x: PWDVA offences are an SLL head; cruelty, kidnapping and dowry death are IPC/BNS heads.

s: Women form only about what share of India's police force?
x: Only 11.7% of police are women, one sign of weak justice delivery along with low conviction and high pendency.

s: In which year was India's first all-women police station set up at Kozhikode, Kerala?
x: The first all-women police station was set up at Kozhikode, Kerala in 1973.

s:
Arrange the following crime heads in descending order of their share among crimes against women in 2023:
A. Assault with intent to outrage modesty
B. Cruelty by husband or relatives
C. Kidnapping and abduction
x: The descending order is cruelty by husband or relatives at 29.8%, kidnapping and abduction at 19.8%, and assault with intent to outrage modesty at 18.7%.

s: In the NCRB Crime in India 2024 data, which crime head was dominant, accounting for about 42% of crimes against women?
o: Assault with intent to outrage modesty
x: Cruelty by husband or relatives was the dominant head in NCRB 2024, at about 42% of crimes against women; it was also the top head in 2023 (29.8%). Kidnapping and abduction (19.8%) and assault on modesty (18.7%) ranked below it in 2023.

s: Which State recorded the highest crime rate against women in 2023?
x: Telangana had the highest crime rate against women in 2023, whereas Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of cases.

s: According to the Crime in India 2023 data, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against women?
x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of crimes against women in 2023. Telangana recorded the highest crime rate, which is a different measure.

s: According to NCRB Crime in India 2024, fraud accounted for about what share of cybercrime cases?
x: Cybercrime crossed 1 lakh cases (1,01,928) for the first time, and 72.6% was fraud; sexual exploitation was only 3.1%.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pendency of cases involving crimes against women — over 90%
x: The rape conviction rate in 2023 was 22.7%, not 42%. About 42% refers to the share of cruelty by husband as a dominant category in 2024.

s: Which group of States accounted for most dowry-death cases according to the cited data?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
West Bengal, Assam, Sikkim and Tripura
x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan accounted for most dowry-death cases in the cited data.

s: According to NCRB data, which State leads in child marriage cases?
x: Assam leads, with 5,267 of 6,038 child marriage cases nationally in 2023.

s: Cyber crimes against women rose by about what percentage between 2017 and 2022?
x: They rose about 239% (stalking, morphing, trolling); 72.6% is the fraud share of cybercrime in 2024.

s: Crime in India 2024 is the first NCRB report to give data under which law?
x: Crime in India 2024, released in May 2026, is the first report with BNS data beside IPC data.

s: What was the rape conviction rate in India in 2023?
x: The rape conviction rate was 22.7% in 2023, down from 27-28% in 2018-22.

s: What was the share of cruelty by husband or relatives in crimes against women in 2023?
x: Cruelty had a 29.8% share in 2023; about 42% is its 2024 share. 19.8% is kidnapping and 18.7% assault.

s: Which State recorded the most trafficking cases in 2024?
x: Telangana recorded the most trafficking cases in 2024.

s: According to Crime in India 2024, which State had the highest violent-crime rate?
x: Crime in India 2024 shows Odisha with the highest rate of violent crime.

s: In which year did cybercrime cases in India cross 1 lakh for the first time, as per NCRB?
x: In 2024 cybercrime cases crossed 1 lakh for the first time (1,01,928, up 17%).

s: According to NCRB Crime in India 2024, how many cases of crimes against women were registered in India?
x: Crime in India 2024 recorded 4,41,534 crimes against women, down 1.5% from about 4.48 lakh in 2023.

s: What was India's crime rate per lakh population in Crime in India 2024, the lowest since 2019?
x: Crime in India 2024 recorded 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes with a crime rate of 418.9 per lakh.

s: What percentage of women were married before attaining 18 years according to NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 reported that 23.3% of women were married before the age of 18. NFHS-4 had recorded 26.8%.

s: According to NFHS-5, what proportion of ever-married women have faced spousal violence?
x: NFHS-5 reported that 32% of ever-married women had faced spousal violence.

s: As per NFHS-4, what percentage of women reported marital rape?
x: NFHS-4 recorded 5.4%; the marital rape exception remains, and the Delhi High Court gave a split verdict on it.

s: According to Census 2011, what was the Child Sex Ratio of India and Andhra Pradesh respectively?
x: The Child Sex Ratio was 918 in India and 944 in Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011.

s: What was India's sex ratio at birth as per NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 recorded a sex ratio at birth of 929, against an overall sex ratio of 1,020 (up from 991 in NFHS-4).

s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 mainly to address the decline in which of the following?
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 to address the declining Child Sex Ratio and related discrimination against girls. It now covers all districts.

s: What was the adult sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh as per Census 2011?
x: Andhra Pradesh's adult sex ratio was 996 against India's 943; its child sex ratio was 944 against India's 918.

s: Which of the following is prohibited by the PCPNDT Act?
o: Prenatal tests for detecting genetic abnormalities
Collection of census data on sex ratio
x: The PCPNDT law bans advertising sex determination, while it permits diagnostic procedures for genetic abnormalities.

s: Under the PCPNDT Act, 1994, prenatal diagnostic techniques are permitted mainly for detecting what?
o: The future educational needs of the child
The economic status of the family
The sex of the foetus for parental choice
x: The PCPNDT Act permits diagnostic procedures for detecting genetic abnormalities, while prohibiting sex selection and prenatal sex determination.

s: What was India's overall sex ratio according to NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 overall sex ratio is 1,020 (NFHS-4: 991); 929 is sex ratio at birth and 918 the 2011 child sex ratio.

s: According to NFHS-5, what share of women aged 18-49 faced physical violence?
x: 29% of women aged 18-49 faced physical violence; 32% of ever-married women faced spousal violence.

s: Which High Court gave a split verdict on the marital rape exception?
x: The Delhi High Court gave a split verdict; the marital rape exception still remains in law.

s: What was India's Child Sex Ratio as per Census 2001?
x: India's Child Sex Ratio fell from 927 in 2001 to 918 in 2011.
